excerpt: A repaired car is often worth less than it was. How diminished value claims work in Georgia and South Carolina, and how an independent appraisal answers the insurer's 17c formula.
keyTakeaways: Diminished value claims recover the loss in vehicle market value after repair. Georgia is one of the strongest DV states (State Farm v. Mabry, 2001; O.C.G.A. § 33-4-7). South Carolina allows third-party DV claims (Newman v. Brown) but not under a standard collision policy (Schulmeyer v. State Farm). An independent appraisal is the best answer to an insurer's 17c number.

faqs.question: What is a diminished value claim?
faqs.answer: A claim for the reduction in vehicle market value after an accident, even after full repairs.

faqs.question: Is Georgia good for DV claims?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under State Farm v. Mabry (Ga. 2001), your own insurer must assess and pay diminished value on a collision or comprehensive claim, and O.C.G.A. § 33-4-7 allows a bad-faith penalty against the at-fault driver's insurer if it refuses a proper demand for 60 days.

faqs.question: Can I file in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: Yes, against the at-fault driver, whose liability insurer pays the claim. South Carolina measures vehicle damage as repair costs plus any remaining loss in value (Newman v. Brown). A standard collision policy does not owe diminished value (Schulmeyer v. State Farm, 2003).

faqs.question: How is diminished value calculated?
faqs.answer: Insurers often use the 17c formula: 10% of the car's NADA retail value, reduced by damage and mileage multipliers. It comes from a Georgia class-action injunction, not from law. An independent appraisal based on comparable sales can show a larger loss.

faqs.question: How much can I recover?
faqs.answer: It depends on the car's pre-accident value, mileage and how severe the damage was. An independent appraisal based on comparable sales puts a figure on your specific loss.

faqs.question: Do I need a lawyer?
faqs.answer: Smaller claims can often be handled yourself, including in magistrate court (up to $15,000 in Georgia, rising to $25,000 on January 1, 2027, and $7,500 in South Carolina). For larger claims, structural damage, or an insurer that will not move, a lawyer can make the formal demand that preserves Georgia's bad-faith penalty.

metaDescription: Recover your repaired car's lost value in Georgia (4 years to sue) or South Carolina (3 years). How DV claims, the 17c formula and appraisals work.
